# The Methods in Practice: The Authors at Work {#showcase}

Every method in this book is a real tool, and the surest proof is that the people who wrote the book have spent their careers using these tools on real problems - measuring pain and depression and curiosity, running clinical trials, wrestling with missing data, arguing about what a number even means. This closing chapter is a **field guide with receipts**: for each family of methods, it points to where the book teaches it *and* to published work where you can watch it do real scientific labor. Consider it both a map and an invitation - read ours, then go make your own.

A note on completeness and honesty: the list below is *selected*, not exhaustive, and it favors publications whose citation details we could verify. A few relevant pieces (a Monte-Carlo study of CFA fit statistics; an IRT calibration paper) are still in preparation and are omitted here rather than cited as finished. That is the same discipline the [case studies](23-sportspage.qmd) preached: claim only what you can stand behind.

## Measurement: Reliability, Validity, and What a Number Means

Taught in [Reliability](10-reliability.qmd) and [Validity](11-validity.qmd). Measurement theory is the authors' signature territory - the argument that a measure is a *claim* to be defended, not a column of numbers to be trusted.

- Sechrest, McKnight, & McKnight [@SechrestMcKnight1996] - *Calibration of measures for psychotherapy outcome studies* (**American Psychologist**). The foundational statement: scores mean nothing until they are calibrated against something real.
- Coan, Allen, & McKnight [@CoanAllenMcKnight2006] - a **capability model** of frontal EEG asymmetry (**Biological Psychology**): reconceiving what an individual-differences measure is measuring.
- Schnyer et al. [@SchnyerMcKnight2005] - building a Chinese-medicine assessment with the **Delphi method** and inter-rater reliability (**J. Alternative & Complementary Medicine**).
- McKnight & Sechrest [@McKnightSechrest2003] - *The use and misuse of the term "experience"* (**Philosophical Psychology**): what happens when a construct is never properly measured.

## IRT, Rasch, and Generalizability Theory

Taught in [Measuring Like Ben Wright](18-rasch.qmd). The authors' item-response work runs unusually deep for a statistics-textbook author - and one paper was co-written with Ben Wright himself.

- Conrad, **Wright**, McKnight, et al. [@ConradWrightMcKnight2004] - *Comparing traditional and Rasch analyses of the Mississippi PTSD Scale* (**J. Applied Measurement**). Yes, that Wright, from the [Rasch chapter](18-rasch.qmd) - reverse-scored items behave badly, and Rasch reveals why.
- McKnight & Babcock-Parziale [@McKnightBabcock2007] - **Rasch plus generalizability theory** in one study of a vision-rehabilitation outcome (**Optometry and Vision Science**).
- Babcock-Parziale, McKnight, & Head [@BabcockMcKnightHead2005] - psychometric equating of two blind-rehabilitation measures (**JRRD**).
- Stroud, McKnight, & Jensen [@StroudMcKnightJensen2004] - using **IRT** to shorten a disability scale without losing information (**The Journal of Pain**).

## Factor Analysis, SEM, and Growth Curves

Taught in [Building a Measure](25-casestudy-curiosity.qmd) (EFA → CFA → invariance). The authors' factor-analytic work leans confirmatory and simulation-flavored.

- Voelkle & McKnight [@VoelkleMcKnight2012] - *One size fits all?* (**Methodology**): a Monte-Carlo comparison of repeated-measures (M)ANOVA and **latent curve modeling** - exactly the [ANOVA-is-a-GLM](16-ANOVAandGLM.qmd) idea, extended into structural models.

## Latent Class and Mixture Models

Taught (as configural profiles/antitypes) in [When the Total Score Hides the Story](24-casestudy-depression.qmd).

- Kashdan, McKnight, Richey, & Hofmann [@KashdanMcKnightRichey2009] - **latent class analysis** uncovering a neglected, risk-prone subtype of social-anxiety disorder in the National Comorbidity Survey (**Behaviour Research and Therapy**). A hidden subgroup a sum score would never find.

## Missing Data

Taught in [Data Cleaning](05-datacleaning.qmd) and [The Data You Didn't Get](26-casestudy-missing.qmd). This is the authoritative slot - one of us wrote the book.

- McKnight, McKnight, Sidani, & Figueredo [@McKnight2007] - *Missing Data: A Gentle Introduction* (**Guilford Press**). The book behind the [missing-data case study](26-casestudy-missing.qmd).
- McKnight & McKnight [@McKnightMcKnight2013] - *Missing data in psychological science*, in the **Oxford Handbook of Research Strategies for Clinical Psychology**.

## Mediation and Moderation

Taught alongside [Multiple Regression](15-MRC.qmd) and the [modern-methods chapter](20-beyond.qmd) (bootstrapped indirect effects).

- McKnight, Afram, Kashdan, Kasle, & Zautra [@McKnightAfram2010] - a **bootstrapped mixed-effects mediation** model: coping self-efficacy as the mechanism between catastrophizing and physical functioning (**J. Behavioral Medicine**). The exact bootstrap-the-indirect-effect logic from [Beyond the Normal Curve](20-beyond.qmd).
- Hofmann, Richey, Kashdan, & McKnight [@HofmannRicheyKashdanMcKnight2009] - anxiety disorders **moderate** the externalizing–substance-use link (**J. Anxiety Disorders**).

## Longitudinal, Multilevel, and the Applied GLM

Taught across [the GLM chapters](12-GLMcovariance.qmd) and [Power](09-statisticalpower.qmd). The authors' clinical-trial and diary work is where the linear model earns its living.

- McKnight, Kasle, Going, et al. [@McKnightOA2010] - a 24-month **randomized controlled trial** of strength training for knee osteoarthritis (**Arthritis Care & Research**).
- Kasle, Wilhelm, McKnight, et al. [@KasleMcKnight2010] - a **prospective** study of mutuality and inflammation in rheumatoid arthritis (**Arthritis Care & Research**).
- Doorley, Kashdan, Alexander, Blalock, & McKnight [@DoorleyKashdanMcKnight2019] - a **daily-diary / multilevel** design on distress tolerance (**Motivation and Emotion**).
- Baer, Kivlahan, Blume, McKnight, & Marlatt [@BaerMcKnight2001] - a **4-year longitudinal** follow-up of a brief-intervention trial (**American Journal of Public Health**).
- Foroughi, Monfort, Paczynski, McKnight, & Greenwood [@ForoughiMcKnight2016] - **placebo effects in cognitive training** (**PNAS**): a design lesson about what a "control" group must control.

## Theory Worth Measuring

Taught implicitly throughout - because the [whole point](intro.qmd) of good measurement is a question worth answering.

- McKnight & Kashdan [@McKnightKashdan2009fcn] - the case for **functional impairment** as the real outcome in depression research (**Clinical Psychology Review**).
- McKnight & Kashdan [@McKnightKashdan2009purpose] - *Purpose in life as a system that creates and sustains health and well-being* (**Review of General Psychology**) - the construct behind the [purpose-and-happiness case study](26-casestudy-missing.qmd).
- Kashdan & McKnight [@KashdanMcKnight2010darker] - *The darker side of social anxiety* (**Current Directions in Psychological Science**).

## Go Make Your Own

That is the map: every method in this book has done real work in the world, and now you have the coordinates to go read it. But the deeper invitation is the one this whole book has been making since the [first page](index.qmd). The tools are not the point. The point is a career's worth of honest questions, carefully measured, honestly modeled, and truthfully reported - some of which you will get wrong, and say so. Read ours. Then go collect your own body of work, and someday write the field guide with *your* receipts in it.
